spec.title: Europa · Beneath the silence
spec.description: An ocean world, a sheet of ice, and questions we are learning how to ask. NASA footage with original artist concepts and a schematic cutaway.

panels.title: Evidence, not a discovery of life

entries.label: Surface
entries.detail: Europa's visible surface is mostly water ice, crossed by dark fractures.

entries.label: Hidden ocean
entries.detail: Magnetic and geological evidence supports a salty ocean below the ice. This film does not depict an observed seafloor.

entries.label: Mission question
entries.detail: Europa Clipper investigates whether Europa has conditions suitable for life.

segments.title: A world of ice
segments.narration: Far from Earth, Jupiter's moon Europa wears a shell of ice. Its fractured surface is the beginning of a much deeper story.

cards.title: Artist's concept
cards.body: The orbital artwork was generated for this film. It is not a spacecraft photograph.

segments.title: Follow the evidence
segments.narration: Spacecraft observations give scientists clues. The surface and Europa's response to Jupiter's magnetic field point toward liquid water hidden below the ice.

cards.title: NASA footage and evidence
cards.body: NASA video introduces Europa. Magnetic measurements are one line of evidence for a salty ocean.

segments.title: An unseen ocean
segments.narration: We have not visited this seafloor. This imagined scene makes the question tangible: could water, chemistry and energy meet in an environment that supports life?

cards.title: Speculative visualization
cards.body: The ocean interior is an artist's concept. No life has been discovered on Europa.

segments.title: Read the layers
segments.narration: Separate the visible ice shell from the inferred ocean and the rocky interior. This diagram is a schematic, not a measurement of their relative thickness.

cards.title: Europa's structure
cards.body: Compare the diagram with NASA's overview and the uncertainties it describes.

segments.title: Ask better questions
segments.narration: Europa Clipper is designed to study this ocean world. Its investigation connects the ice, chemistry and geology to a broader question about habitability.

cards.title: Mission purpose
cards.body: Habitability means conditions that could support life. It is different from detecting living organisms.

segments.title: Fractures as clues
segments.narration: Europa's fractured ice records a changing surface. Scientists study its patterns to understand the relationship between the shell and the ocean below.

segments.title: Evidence below the surface
segments.narration: The case for a hidden ocean comes from multiple observations. Its depth, chemistry and exchange with the surface remain research questions.

cards.title: What supports an ocean?
cards.body: Read the magnetic and geological evidence rather than treating this visualization as a photograph.
